proposals.before: He rose in due course to the post of lecturer in the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: He rose in due course to the post of Expositor-in-waiting.
proposals.reason: 侍講學士 is a Hanlin Academy expositor rank, not an office in the Grand Secretariat (內閣); the next sentence correctly promotes him to 內閣學士.

proposals.before: He was promoted in succession to lecturer in the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was promoted in succession to Expositor-in-waiting.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 侍講學士 is not Grand Secretariat lecturer.

proposals.before: While in Guangxi Fu had captured the rebellious Miao leader Mo Dongwang and placed him in Tianhe County prison. The case was unfinished when Fu was transferred to govern Zhili.
proposals.after: While in Guangxi, Fu had captured the rebellious Miao leader Mo Dongwang and placed him in Tianhe County prison. The case was unfinished when Fu was transferred to govern Zhili.
proposals.reason: Insert comma after the place phrase so 'Guangxi Fu' is not read as a fused personal name.

proposals.before: I summoned Ting to an audience, but he said one should not associate with princes and declined to come. For that I held him in esteem.
proposals.after: I summoned Ting to an audience; Ting said one should not associate with princes and declined to come. For that I held him in esteem.
proposals.reason: Chinese repeats 珽 as subject of the refusal; idiomatic fused the second Ting into 'he', obscuring the named referent.

proposals.before: Before long Fu reported that he had fallen ill; within a few days he was dead.
proposals.after: Before long Fu reported that Seshei had fallen ill; within a few days he was dead.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遘病…即死 refers to Seshei under Fu's custody, not Fu; idiomatic 'he' is ambiguous and can be read as Fu.

proposals.before: Ting humiliated Chongqing Prefect Jiang Xingren, who in anger killed himself. Ting reported that he had died of illness. Gengyao impeached him; the emperor questioned and rebuked him repeatedly before he finally confessed.
proposals.after: Ting humiliated Chongqing Prefect Jiang Xingren, who in anger killed himself. Ting reported that Jiang had died of illness. Gengyao impeached him; the emperor questioned and rebuked him repeatedly before he finally confessed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以病卒聞 refers to reporting Jiang Xingren's death as illness; idiomatic 'he' is ambiguous between Ting and Jiang.

proposals.before: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital for interrogation. The emperor read a book by Gengyao's client, provincial graduate Wang Jingqi, which recorded that while governing Sichuan Ting had received bribes from Kuizhou Prefect Cheng Rusi and recommended him first in official conduct.
proposals.after: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital for interrogation. The emperor read a book by Gengyao's client, provincial graduate Wang Jingqi, which recorded that while Ting was governing Sichuan he had received bribes from Kuizhou Prefect Cheng Rusi and recommended him first in official conduct.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'Sichuan Ting' fuses place and person; Chinese 珽撫四川時 clearly means when Ting governed Sichuan.

proposals.before: In the sixth year, Prince of Xin De Zhao, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.
proposals.after: In the sixth year, De Zhao, Prince of Xin, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 信郡王德昭 is title plus personal name; English fused them as "Prince of Xin De Zhao" as if De Zhao were part of the toponym.

proposals.before: In the sixth year, Prince of Xin De Zhao, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence, warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.
proposals.after: In the sixth year, De Zhao, Prince of Xin, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence, warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.
proposals.reason: Same name/title fusion error as in the idiomatic field for 信郡王德昭.

proposals.before: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Prince of Ping Fupeng treated him with considerable respect, and Jishi continued lecturing and writing without pause.
proposals.after: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Fupeng, Prince of Ping, treated him with considerable respect, and Jishi continued lecturing and writing without pause.
proposals.reason: Chinese 平郡王福彭 is title plus name; English fused them as "Prince of Ping Fupeng".

proposals.before: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Prince of Shuncheng Xibao, citing Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning as slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment and requested punishment.
proposals.after: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Xibao, Prince of Shuncheng, citing Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning as slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment and requested punishment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 順承郡王錫保 is title plus name; English fused them as "Prince of Shuncheng Xibao".

proposals.before: but as for Long Sheng, everyone says he should not be used, yet he has still not been dismissed.
proposals.after: but as for Longsheng, everyone says he should not be used, yet he has still not been dismissed.
proposals.reason: Chinese personal name 隆升 should not be spaced as two English words "Long Sheng".

proposals.before: Not only has Long Sheng not been dismissed; men such as Wang Shijun, who treated tax increases as land reclamation and wantonly harmed the central provinces, also requested establishing a shrine of worthy and good men for Tian Wenjing.
proposals.after: Not only has Longsheng not been dismissed; men such as Wang Shijun, who treated tax increases as land reclamation and wantonly harmed the central provinces, also requested establishing a shrine of worthy and good men for Tian Wenjing.
proposals.reason: Same spacing error for personal name 隆升 as in the prior sentence.

proposals.before: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he contended were wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.
proposals.after: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he argued had been wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.
proposals.reason: English 'those he contended were wronged were' is ungrammatical and obscure; the Chinese means those Fu contended had been wronged.

proposals.before: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he contended were wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.
proposals.after: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he argued had been wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.
proposals.reason: Same ungrammatical phrasing as the idiomatic field; repair to match the Chinese sense of contending they were wronged.

proposals.before: he also incited Jishi to lodge open memorial impeachments; they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
proposals.after: Ting also incited Jishi to lodge open memorial impeachments; they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
proposals.reason: Silent subject after 世宗疑珽… is Ting (珽), not the Yongzheng Emperor; the emperor would not incite overthrow of Wenjing, his favored official.

proposals.before: he also incited Jishi to open memorial impeachment, they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
proposals.after: Ting also incited Jishi to lodge an open memorial of impeachment; they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise uses ambiguous 'he' and weaker grammar; subject is Ting continuing from the prior clause about 珽.
